summary: The Rincon Mountain tower and cabin were moved by helicopter to Nordhoff Peak around 1950; no source describes the Rincon site today.

corrections.why: The FFLOS Nordhoff Peak page and a 2012 blog post say the tower and cabin were moved from Rincon Mountain to Nordhoff Peak around 1950.
The FFLOS page calls the structure moved from Rincon Mountain an existing tower and cabin, while the FFLA list types the Rincon site as Ground. Not verified on the ground; check before applying.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list marks the Rincon site gone; the FFLOS and blog sources say the structure left Rincon Mountain. Both can be true of the Rincon site.

notes_for_editor: Nothing in the sources gives a build date, design or history for the Rincon Mountain site itself; the Weebly page has only a county heading. The FFLOS and Carey sources agree that the Nordhoff Peak structure came from Rincon Mountain around 1950. The FFLOS page gives no county, so identity rests on the name and the FFLA county listing. The kind correction is unverified. Carey's 2012 post is a blog; its steel-frame remark is the only source on the current state at Nordhoff Peak.
